subject: Biology
title: Human Health and Disease
summary: Health is a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being. Diseases are infectious (caused by pathogens — bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoans, helminths) or non-infectious (cancer).
Immunity is innate (non-specific barriers present at birth) or acquired (specific, with memory — B cells make antibodies, T cells give cell-mediated immunity). Vaccination uses this memory.
Allergies, autoimmunity (rheumatoid arthritis) and AIDS (HIV attacks helper T cells) are failures or attacks of the immune system. Cancer is uncontrolled cell division (loss of contact inhibition).
Drug and alcohol abuse (opioids, cannabinoids, coca alkaloids) damage health; adolescence is the most vulnerable period, and prevention is better than cure.

formulas.name: Bacterial diseases
formulas.formula: typhoid — Salmonella typhi (Widal test, intestinal perforation);  pneumonia — Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae (alveoli fill with fluid; lips and nails grey to bluish)

formulas.name: Viral and fungal diseases
formulas.formula: common cold — rhinoviruses (nose and respiratory passage, not lungs);  ringworm — Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton (dry scaly skin lesions; heat and moisture help growth)

formulas.name: Protozoan diseases
formulas.formula: malaria — Plasmodium vivax, P. malariae, P. falciparum (most serious, cerebral malaria);  amoebiasis — Entamoeba histolytica (houseflies carry cysts; mucus and blood clots in stool)

formulas.name: Plasmodium life cycle
formulas.formula: sporozoites (infective stage) enter via female Anopheles bite → liver (asexual multiplication) → RBCs (burst, release haemozoin → chills and high fever every 3–4 days) → gametocytes → mosquito gut (fertilisation) → sporozoites in salivary glands
formulas.note: Sexual reproduction happens in the mosquito; humans are the intermediate host.

formulas.name: Helminth diseases
formulas.formula: ascariasis — Ascaris (eggs in contaminated soil, water, vegetables; internal bleeding, muscular pain, intestinal blockage);  filariasis/elephantiasis — Wuchereria bancrofti, W. malayi (female Culex mosquito; lymphatic vessels of lower limbs)

formulas.name: Innate immunity barriers
formulas.formula: physical (skin, mucus);  physiological (stomach acid, saliva, tears);  cellular (neutrophils, monocytes, NK cells, macrophages);  cytokine (interferons from virus-infected cells)

formulas.name: Antibody structure
formulas.formula: 4 polypeptide chains: 2 heavy + 2 light (H₂L₂), held together by disulphide bonds;  antigen-binding site = variable region at the N-terminal ends (tips of the Y);  constant region at the C-terminal end;  types IgA, IgM, IgE, IgG (IgG crosses placenta; IgA in colostrum)

formulas.name: Active vs passive immunity
formulas.formula: active: body makes antibodies (infection or vaccination) — slow, long-lasting;  passive: ready-made antibodies given (mother's milk, placenta, anti-tetanus serum, snake antivenom) — quick, short-lived

formulas.name: Lymphoid organs
formulas.formula: primary: bone marrow (all blood cells, B cells mature) and thymus (T cells mature);  secondary: spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches, appendix, MALT (~50% of lymphoid tissue)

formulas.name: HIV/AIDS
formulas.formula: retrovirus (RNA → reverse transcriptase → DNA);  enters macrophages (HIV factory) and helper T cells (T_H) → T_H count falls → opportunistic infections;  diagnosis by ELISA;  treated (not cured) with anti-retroviral drugs

formulas.name: Cancer basics
formulas.formula: loss of contact inhibition;  benign tumour (stays confined to its original location, little damage) vs malignant (a mass of proliferating neoplastic/tumour cells that grow very rapidly, invade and damage surrounding tissue, and spread by metastasis);  carcinogens: ionising radiation (X-rays, gamma), non-ionising UV, chemicals (tobacco smoke), oncogenic viruses (proto-oncogenes → oncogenes)

formulas.name: Cancer detection and treatment
formulas.formula: detection: biopsy, histopathology, blood/bone marrow tests (increased cell counts in leukaemia), X-ray, CT, MRI (cancers of internal organs), antibodies, molecular biology;  treatment: surgery, radiation, chemotherapy (drugs kill cancerous cells; side effects like hair loss, anaemia), immunotherapy (biological response modifiers such as α-interferon activate the immune system to destroy the tumour)

formulas.name: Drugs of abuse
formulas.formula: opioids: morphine (sedative, painkiller), heroin/smack (diacetylmorphine — depressant) from Papaver somniferum;  cannabinoids from Cannabis sativa (marijuana, hashish, charas, ganja) — cardiovascular effects;  coca alkaloid (cocaine/coke/crack) from Erythroxylum coca — interferes with dopamine transport, euphoria;  Atropa belladonna and Datura are hallucinogenic

formulas.name: Allergy
formulas.formula: exaggerated response to allergens (pollen, mites); IgE antibodies; mast cells release histamine and serotonin;  treated with anti-histamines, adrenaline, steroids

examples.title: Chills in malaria
examples.problem: What causes the chills and high fever in malaria?
examples.solution: Rupture of RBCs releases a toxic substance, haemozoin, which causes chills and high fever recurring every three to four days.

examples.title: Colostrum
examples.problem: Why is colostrum important for a newborn?
examples.solution: It contains abundant IgA antibodies that give the baby passive immunity.

examples.title: Snakebite treatment
examples.problem: What is given after a snake bite, and what type of immunity is it?
examples.solution: Antivenom — preformed antibodies against the snake venom; this is passive immunisation.

examples.title: Why AIDS weakens immunity
examples.problem: Why do AIDS patients suffer infections that healthy people resist?
examples.solution: HIV destroys helper T lymphocytes, which coordinate both antibody and cell-mediated responses; immunity collapses and opportunistic infections (Mycobacterium, Toxoplasma, fungi, viruses) take hold.

examples.title: Organ rejection
examples.solution: Cell-mediated immunity (T lymphocytes). Tissue and blood group matching and lifelong immunosuppressants reduce rejection.

topics.title: Maintaining health
topics.explain: Balanced diet, personal hygiene, regular exercise, yoga, awareness about diseases, vaccination, proper disposal of waste, control of vectors and safe food and water.

topics.title: Prevention and control of infectious diseases
topics.explain: Personal hygiene and public hygiene: proper disposal of waste and excreta, periodic cleaning and disinfection of water reservoirs. For vector-borne diseases (malaria, filariasis, dengue, chikungunya), control mosquitoes: avoid stagnant water, use mosquito nets, introduce Gambusia fish in ponds (feeds on larvae), spray insecticides.

topics.title: Vaccination and immunisation
topics.explain: A vaccine contains inactivated or weakened pathogens or antigenic proteins; it generates memory B and T cells. Recombinant DNA technology allows antigenic polypeptides to be made in bacteria or yeast (hepatitis B vaccine from yeast).

topics.title: Autoimmunity
topics.explain: Due to genetic and unknown reasons, the body attacks self-cells — e.g. rheumatoid arthritis.

topics.title: Adolescence and drug abuse
topics.explain: Adolescence (12–18 years) is a vulnerable period. Causes: curiosity, adventure, excitement, peer pressure, academic stress, unstable family. Effects: reckless behaviour, vandalism, violence; heavy drinking damages the liver (cirrhosis) and nervous system; drug users injecting intravenously risk AIDS and hepatitis B. Anabolic steroids cause masculinisation in females and reduced sperm count in males.

topics.title: Prevention of drug and alcohol abuse
topics.explain: Avoid undue peer pressure, education and counselling, seeking help from parents and peers, looking for danger signs (drop in academic performance, isolation, aggressive behaviour) and seeking professional and medical help.

ratta: Typhoid — Salmonella typhi (Widal);  pneumonia — Streptococcus, Haemophilus.
Common cold — rhinoviruses;  ringworm — Microsporum, Trichophyton, Epidermophyton.
Malaria: female Anopheles, haemozoin;  P. falciparum most serious.
HIV: retrovirus, reverse transcriptase, kills T_H; ELISA.
Neoplastic (malignant) cells: proliferating mass, very rapid growth, invade surrounding tissue;  benign = confined.
Leukaemia: blood cell count UP;  chemo kills cancer cells;  α-interferon = biological response modifier.
Antibody: H and L chains joined by S–S bonds;  antigen binding at N-terminal (variable), constant region at C-terminal.
